_comment: Template for the file the weekly routine writes to data/weekly_inputs.json before running build_report.py. Every field is optional - build_report.py degrades gracefully, scoring what it has and flagging the rest. Delete the _comment keys in real output.

spx_current._comment: Current S&P 500 index level. The Shiller CSV is monthly and lags by weeks, so without this the whole report is scored off last month's close. Same calendar month replaces that month's close; a later month is appended.

cape_web._comment: Current Shiller CAPE cross-check. Preferred for the headline; the value computed from the Shiller CSV is shown alongside it.

buffett_indicator._comment: Total US market cap / GDP, in percent (e.g. 212 means 212%).

fiscal._comment: deficit_pct_gdp is a positive number for a deficit. Both fields fall back to FRED (FYFSGDA188S, GFDEGDQ188S) when omitted.

fred_fallback._comment: Only used when the FRED API and the local cache both fail. UNITS: DGS10 in percent (4.25), T10Y2Y in percentage points (0.55), BAMLH0A0HYM2 in BASIS POINTS (271) - note the bps unit differs from FRED's own percent scale, because the framework anchors are in bps.

cpi_fallback._comment: Current CPI year-over-year run-rate, percent. Only used when FRED CPIAUCSL is unavailable, to extend the Shiller CPI column past its last valid month so recent real prices are not dropped.

_curve_post_inversion_comment: true if the 10y-2y curve has been inverted at any point in the trailing 36 months. Only consulted when the FRED T10Y2Y series is unavailable; worth ~0.7 of score, so set it explicitly when you supply fred_fallback.T10Y2Y.

sentiment_updates._comment: One entry per roster member with something NEW in the last 2 weeks. Omit quiet names entirely - omission leaves last week's scores untouched. Names must match data/sentiment_baseline.json exactly.
sentiment_updates.name: Dalio

statement.summary: one line, what he actually said or filed

reading_list.why: one line tying it to a specific indicator or roster name
